subject.title: refactor(memory-wiki): move compiled cache to plugin state

question: Should `registerMemoryPromptPreparation(...)` be accepted as a public, non-exclusive plugin SDK lifecycle contract for asynchronous prompt-state loading across all agent and context-engine entry points?
rationale: The mechanical CLI repair is clear, but making this lifecycle hook public determines the durable plugin API and its compatibility obligations beyond Memory Wiki.

options.title: Adopt the lifecycle API with complete coverage
options.body: Keep the registration, repair every production prompt entry point, and document its owner-validation and immutable-run-snapshot contract.

options.title: Keep the refactor plugin-local
options.body: Avoid the new SDK surface and use an existing owner-local preparation seam if one can preserve synchronous prompt assembly without exposing a general lifecycle hook.

options.title: Pause API acceptance
options.body: Hold this PR until an owner defines the intended async prompt-state extension model and its compatibility policy.

recommendation.title: Adopt the lifecycle API with complete coverage
recommendation.body: Keep the registration, repair every production prompt entry point, and document its owner-validation and immutable-run-snapshot contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history ties steipete to the complete proposed lifecycle and cache-owner design, although current-main ownership evidence is limited.
